title: Keep one bad partner file from stopping the points ledger

blocks.text: The loyalty service imports partner files into its points ledger on a few worker threads, one file at a time. Two incidents last month:

items: A café partner sent a file that would have taken a member below zero. The file was rejected, as it should be, and from then on no other file was imported until someone restarted the service.
During a deploy, the service waited out its whole shutdown timeout: two workers were waiting for the ledger behind a long airline import, and the interrupts the deploy sent them changed nothing.

blocks.text: Write `importFile` in `src/main/java/practice/PointsLedger.java`. It applies the file with the `applyAll` method that is already there, holding the ledger's lock. A rejected file must leave the ledger ready for the next one, and its `IllegalArgumentException` must still reach the caller. A worker that is interrupted while it waits for the ledger must stop waiting, import nothing, and end with `InterruptedException`. About five lines.
The tests run the workers on threads of their own and hold the ledger's lock themselves to keep a worker waiting.

cases.says: two files imported from two worker threads both reach the balances
after a file is rejected, another worker can still import the next file
a worker that waits for the ledger stops waiting when it is interrupted, and imports nothing
a worker interrupted while waiting for the ledger ends with InterruptedException, not with another exception

origin.section: lock() Waits Until It Gets the Lock; tryLock and lockInterruptibly Can Give Up

concepts: lockInterruptibly() and tryLock go before the try, so that a failed attempt never runs unlock(): inside it, IllegalMonitorStateException replaces InterruptedException, or an outer hold is silently lost.
lock() keeps waiting through an interrupt, while lockInterruptibly() answers it with InterruptedException and doesn't take the lock.
Nothing releases a ReentrantLock but unlock(): an exception, the end of a task or of the thread leaves it held, so the unlock goes in a finally after a lock() taken before the try.
